en: The Eight Verses on Kṛṣṇa
I worship the Nandanaṇdana, the sole ornament of Vraja, the destroyer of all sins, who eternally delights the hearts of his devotees;
he whose head is crowned with a beautiful cluster of peacock feathers and who holds a melodious flute in his hand.
I bow to Kṛṣṇanāgara, an ocean of the theater of love.
I bow to the lotus-eyed one, who releases the pride of the mind, whose large eyes are tremulous, who has dispelled the grief of the cowherds,
who bears the mountain upon his lotus-like hand, and who is beautiful with his smiling glance.
I bow to the elephant of Kṛṣṇa, who shatters the pride of Mahendra. || 2 ||
I bow to Kṛṣṇa, who is difficult to attain, whose earrings are made of Kadamba buds, whose cheeks are beautifully rounded, who is the sole beloved of the women of Vraja,
and who is accompanied by Yaśodā, who shares his joy, along with the cowherds and Nanda.
I bow to the leader of the Gopas, who is endowed with splendor and is the sole bestower of happiness. || 3 ||
I ever bow to the child of Nanda, who holds his own lotus feet within my mind, who wears a garland of sages,
who dries up all defects, and who nourishes the entire world.
I bow to him who delights in Nanda and who is the object of the minds of all the cowherds. || 4 ||
I bow to the one who brings down the burden of the earth, the helmsman of the ocean of existence, the youth of Yaśomatī, the thief of the mind;
whose beautiful glances possess the grace of a wave, and who is ever united with his virtuous consort.
Day by day, I bow again and again to the one born of Nanda. || 5 ||
I bow to the son of Gopa, the mine of virtues, the source of happiness, the treasury of compassion, the one devoted to mercy, the destroyer of the enemies of the gods,
the youthful lover of the cowherd girls, and the one ever-eager for new pastimes.
I bow to Meghasundara, whose garment shines with the brilliance of lightning.
I bow to the delighter of all the cowherds, who brings singular joy to the lotus of my heart; he dwells within the forest grove, resplendent like the gracious sun,
the granter of every desire, whose beautiful glances are arrows of charm.
I bow to the Lord of the Grove, who is accompanied by the flute-singer Rasālava.
I bow to Him who reclines upon the charming bed of the hearts of clever cowherd girls in the forest grove, who drinks from the flames of the forest fire,
who is colored with the loveliness of youth, and who is beautifully adorned as the collyrium for the eyes.
I bow to the one who liberated the lordly elephant and who sports with Śrī.
Whenever, however, and in whatever manner it may be, let the sacred narrations of Kṛṣṇa be sung by me at all times; may grace thus be bestowed.
That man who, having studied and recited these two sets of eight *pramāṇikā* verses—
In birth after birth, he shall possess excellent devotion toward the Son of Nanda.
Thus ends the Śrīkṛṣṇāṣṭaka composed by the venerable Śaṅkarācārya.
May this be offered unto Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
